newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet chief expects government approval soon.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet chief expects government approval soon.

text.p: The president of ValuJet Airlines said on Tuesday he expected the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) to issue approval soon for the low-fare carrier to resume flights, finding it managerially and financially fit.
"We believe we will get a final order and we think that that will come in the not too distant future, but I cannot possibly tell you exactly when that will be," said Lewis Jordan.
The department issued a show cause order Aug. 29, "tentatively finding ValuJet fit to fly" but invited public comment on its findings and conclusions.
"They could decide to order evidentiary hearings," Jordan told a press club luncheon. "We believe that is not the choice that they will take, based on the reading of the show cause order."

He said the airline will initially serve Atlanta and four other cities, but he was waiting for DOT approval before revealing routes or fares. "We hope to announce those within the next week," he said.
Jordan said ValuJet will continue to promote itself as "fun and friendly" but may expand its advertising beyond print, radio and billboards and move into television.
"What you'll really see from an advertising standpoint is a rather limited ad budget. We will be promoting primarily price and destination," he said.

ValuJet stopped operating in June after its maintenance procedures and operations were scrutinized by the federal government following the May 11 crash of Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades that killed 110 people.
